newsitem.title: ITALY: Australia wants new farm trade reform in WTO talks.
newsitem.headline: Australia wants new farm trade reform in WTO talks.

text.p: Australia called on Thursday for new farm liberalisation in the next round of world trade reforms, saying this should be a topic of a December trade meeting.

"When we meet next month in Singapore for the first ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation, we would do well to recognise the contribution that further trade liberalisation must make if we are to succeed in our task of ensuriing sustainable food security," primary industries minister John Anderson told a U.N. food summit.
The conference is expected to review the six-year Uruguay Round trade pact reached in 1994 and set the pace for new trade negotiations due to begin in 1999.

Australia, initially backed by the United States, was a staunch supporter of ripping down all barriers to free trade in the lengthy and often bitter Uruguay Round negotiations, but some trade tools like export subsidies remained.
Saying it does not subsidise its huge farm exports, Australia has repeatedly attacked subsidies that are still available to Europe and the United States under the pact.
Washington and the European Union agreed to limit and then gradually reduce the subsidies from last year as part of the gobal trade deal.
